boundary: Provider-owned shell executor; command/output rendering and command approvals are wired.
Provider-owned process input; not a UI to manage all provider background terminals.
Provider file editing with diff rendering; modern file-change approvals are supported.
Provider image inspection; Sele can display viewed-image output.
Tool execution belongs to Codex; Sele displays the plan. This does not activate plan mode.
Sele handles item/tool/requestUserInput and displays questions.
Asynchronous agent question messages are collected and answered.
A recognized display name does not establish an install/authentication continuation flow.
Provider goal tools depend on runtime availability; Sele integrates goal get/set/clear APIs, with lifecycle limitations.
Provider Code Mode executor. Nested presentation recognizes a subset of namespaces.
Provider delegation can run; transcript inspection is integrated. Direct subagent management is partial.
Provider clock/sleep tools depend on runtime availability; Sele answers the separate currentTime/read client callback.
Provider/backend tools can run when available. No promise of all first-party rich result widgets.
Provider/image tools and skills are conditional; generated-media display exists.
Provider-owned MCP invocation; generic forms, URLs and supported native verification have UI. Specialized strict review, credential enrollment and custom widgets remain incomplete.
Provider-hosted resource APIs can be available; no native Sele resource browser.

family: MCP custom UI; Apps SDK widgets
boundary: Shared isolated MCP Apps host and Codex/Copilot bridges are implemented. Other runtime bridges and proprietary widget APIs remain unavailable.
Sele implements the in-app browser transport. Requires a compatible installed OpenAI runtime.
Sele provides Linux native screenshot/input tools with explicit Settings connection. X11 is tested privately; live Wayland and other OS native backends remain limited.

family: Hosted Sites, Space, office and other plugin tools
boundary: Access depends on installed/authenticated tools and backend eligibility. A skill/tool name alone is not proof of parity.
Explicitly registered host tools can execute through item/tool/call with argument validation and structured results. Private Desktop implementations are not included.
